notes.title: Announce new game: Railborn
notes.notes:
Friends! We need to talk. Sit down with me. 

Parkasaurus was our first game as a new studio, and will always be #1 in our hearts. This especially means the community and all the encouragement and support we received. While we plan to [b]return to the Parkasaurus universe[/b] - in the meantime we have been working on a new game. This new game may seem very different from Parkasaurus - but is actually born from it!

[h3]Our new game is [b]Railborn [/b]and we'd love for you and your friends you to give us a Wishlist. <3[/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2340970/Railborn

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/e9b9b491486fd3a4fb16d78e51cbbbd741467c56.png[/img]

How are these games related you ask? Let me tell you! We brought all our care and love for biomes and the environment from [b]Parkasaurus[/b] over to [b]Railborn[/b]. Collecting plants, building out railcars to have the perfect balance for each biome will be a major aspect of the game. There is more, but I don't want to bore you with all the similarities yet.

[b]Railborn[/b] is a fresh new adventure for us. As you probably know Washbear is a 2 person studio - and we make games for passion, and this is what our hearts were calling. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/72dd631b7ddb4eb3b85540b91e9655728506b5df.gif[/img]

So how you can help us our? You know what I'm going to ask: 

[b]Please - Wishlist [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2340970/Railborn]Railborn[/url], and then copy that Steam link above and paste it to your friends asking them to checkout the game and Wishlist. [/b]

As always we want you on this journey with us so please join our Discord or any other socials! <3

notes.title: Update #61: 2.0 Sea Monsters
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/f4c5b9fd21546599e7c48911cff0e7c39ca28a27.png[/img]
Friends – Update 2.0 Sea Monsters is upcoming. I thought to discuss what everyone will see. Just a reminder:
[list]
[*]If you have any Update or DLC questions, or [b]just want to say hi (we love this)[/b] – please make a post [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/591460/discussions/0/3455968685016858136/]here on our forums[/url]
[*][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1931130]Throw us a wishlist for the available Sea Monster DLC, it helps pump us up![/url]
[/list]
On with the show!
[list]
[*] Water Toys
[*] Hats
[*] Experimental Controller support
[*] Quality of Life
[*] DLC Available
[/list]

[h1]Water Toys[/h1]
Dinos love toys! We figured why not let [b]all[/b] the dinosaurs enjoy playing with water toys. Therefore all our news toys can be enjoyed by dinos on land and monsters in the sea.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/48671575a23f7768165e7edefdfd79c3671d1553.gif[/img]


[h1]Hats[/h1]
I suppose our logic about Water Toys also applies to Hats. Real talk – I find the 6 new hats so freakingly hilarious on the Theropods I had to make them available to all. If this game isn’t about the joys of life then what is ya know?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/4fccc75d8a7a7ac605c2c65ae60ab2267a5dccb0.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/93db0a97f5085530eb1ee3f72eeecea14510de93.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/f5e002537c41eb35837c1b797bc559d280cb8e28.png[/img]


[h1]Experimental Controller support[/h1]
Finally! For those who like to lounge back and play Parkasaurus with a controller, now you can. Why do we call it “experimental”? Wellll, because there might be a few hiccups still. The cursor now becomes center screen locked which makes building and movement in the game much easier. In fact, I find myself faster in a lot of aspects of the game when using the controller
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/4b5f83f8f3291a227bd9a83ef21074bc34886944.png[/img]


[h1]Quality of Life[/h1]
A few notable [b]quality of life[/b] additions in this Sea Monsters update:

[b]UI goes to 125%[/b]
Yes – we were aware for quite a while the UI could be difficult for some people to read. I just wanted to make a quick note here; if increasing UI size was easy we of course would have done it a long time ago. The reality is that for a game like ours, increasing UI is a really tough feature; languages break, UI breaks, and this requires weeks of testing on our part. Of course, we love our community and you’re all worth it! Just that there are only two of us so we sometimes can’t fix everything, or fix it right away.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/6f8c3c5be7ee02a290e2593aefaf23aaf118bc17.gif[/img]

[b]Reduced GPU Usage when V-Sync is off[/b]
You either get this or you don’t. For most players this was a non-factor, but for the few that had V-Sync off the game really put stress on your poor machines. Fixed!

[b]Max people park 300 to 600[/b]

notes.title: Update #56: Nintendo Switch & PC
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/94a86b82132c05b036ce229fa6fd58e2daf7f3e0.png[/img]

Big news friends! [i]Parkasaurus[/i] is coming to the Nintendo Switch [b]early 2022[/b]! 
Bringing [i]Parkasaurus[/i] over was a challenge the two of us had always wanted to do ourselves. Playing the game on the Switch feels pretty fantastic – and I don’t think anyone else would have given the same love to the port as we did. Wait wait wait, so how does this relate to the PC/Steam version? Well, the controller support required for the Switch (a TON of work) is coming to Steam, along with some other cool tidbits I thought to talk about:


[list]
[*] Fence helper 
[*] Guest skeleton optimization
[*] Multi-threading NavMesh
[*] Controller Support
[/list]


[h1]Fence helper[/h1]
In the video, one can see two [b]fence helpers[/b]. The blue bar that appears showing how the wall aligns is currently in the game. We now added a [b]floating[/b] tile that helps the player not lose track of the cursor location. This makes creating fences with a controller or mouse snappier and quicker. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/485f445f7dad5d7084610c3a987bb0b6a780a4dd.gif[/img]


[h1]Guest skeleton optimization[/h1]
Who knew the skeleton in the models of the guests took up so much computing power! Maybe some of you knew. Each guest had an entire animation skeleton that the game had to keep track of. Multiply this by 200, 300 guests, and that is a lot of wasted CPU! Now all our skeletal animation was converted to vertex animation so the GPU could help out. This means more guests on screen, which also means we can raise (or remove) the guest cap. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/a1002c72012a4bf4ea4031b5ccbf321b5e73f870.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/8cc40cb42b07358a08b97e8c4301bd3f5477f481.png[/img]


[h1]Multi-threading NavMesh[/h1]
We’ve improved the rebuilding that occurs every time an object is placed in [b]Parkasaurus[/b]. The game is broken up into regions that get activated more or less depending on the point of view of the player. This results in a much snappier and lag-free experience building the perfect park. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/de70d6c227136694176553cc05b128241190bc2a.gif[/img]


[h1]Controller Support[/h1]
Everyone said controller support was a lot of work. Did we listen? NO! Was it a lot of work? YES!
Adding controller support to us meant more than just being able to play [b]Parkasaurus[/b] with a controller – we wanted the experience to feel as good if not better than keyboard + mouse. We underestimated how complex the interactions are between all our UI windows that have to be solved with a controller. The video below looks simple, but we had to decide and work on the ordering opening/closing windows. Phew.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/330fecdb867513c7a31bd962d4424343887123c5.gif[/img]


Now be sure to tell your Switch friends about Parkasaurus. 😊 We’ll post again when the game is available.

Currently in [i]Parkasaurus[/i] there are 4 [b]tiers[/b] of dinos: Imperfect, Uncommon, Rare and Epic. Now the [b]Info[/b] pane on your guests reveals the [b]Dinosaur Variety[/b] experienced by your guest in addition to the total number of dinosaur seen. If a guest has seen [b]too many[/b] dinosaurs of a certain tier they become bored, and [b]donate less[/b].

In the picture above the guest has seen 1 [b]Uncommon[/b] dino, 2 [b]Rare[/b] dino, and 1 [b]Epic[/b] dino. No boredom!

[h1]Dino Food[/h1]
Happy March! (whoah slow down 2020). Our upcoming patch has a few changes involving [b]dinosaur food[/b] that I’d like to chat about. Our motivation was to provide players with a few different strategies when choosing how to feed their dinosaurs, both in ways to save money, and also ways to improve their dinos well being. 
[img] https://media.giphy.com/media/J4tCWwfiDk48q29ozI/giphy.gif [/img]
[list]
[*] Food Specialties
[*] Food Slots
[*] Feeder Bonuses
[*] Translation Help - Localizor!
[*] PTR up this weekend
[/list]

[h1] Food Specialties[/h1]
[img] https://i.imgur.com/p3eqsTSh.png [/img]
Are you interested in saving a few dollars when feeding your dinosaurs? Now you can buy them food appropriate for their size. If your dinos happen to large, then buy food that is suited for large dinos. The benefit to this is foods specific to a dino size are much cheaper than the generic food. For example, [b]Tree Leaves[/b] are half the price of generic [b]Plants[/b]. 
[img] https://media.giphy.com/media/USUpfxZfAQ1F3ENEiX/giphy.gif [/img]
Your total food inventory can now be found hovering over the [b]Vegetarian[/b] and [b]Meat[/b] icons.

 [h1]Food Slots[/h1]
[img] https://media.giphy.com/media/ZZrBgCAZMVmvf6EdwS/giphy.gif [/img]
You assign each feeder what food to be filled with through the feeder info pane. By default, feeders are assigned to be filled with the generic Vegetarian (Plant) or Meat food (Fresh Meat) that are suitable for all dinosaur sizes. Selecting a [b]food specialty[/b] means your Veterinarian now fills the feeder with this food instead of the generic food.
Just be careful! Dinosaurs will ignore a [b]food specialty[/b] not appropriate for their size. For example, above I have my Veterinarian filling the feeder with [b]Grass[/b] that I know is suitable for small dinosaurs like my Minmi.

[h1] Feeder Bonuses [/h1]
[img] https://i.imgur.com/pbDeYz7h.jpg [/img]
Did you not all feeders are built equal? Feeders currently have two types of bonuses:
[list]
[*] Capacity: These feeders can hold more food so your Veterinarians do not need to return as often
[*] Health: These feeders provide a Health bonus every time used by a dinosaur.
The bonuses on the feeders can be found at the bottom of their descriptions.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/b529f5b86a9852f0d055b82b6f38f9d6f6422762.jpg[/img]

[h1]End of Day[/h1]
Since [i]Parksaurus[/i] entered Early Access the most contentious aspect of the game has been how we handle the [b]end of day[/b]. The two of us have always envisioned [i]Parksaurus[/i] having a day-night cycle, this made sense to us since we wanted seasons, places for dinosaurs to sleep, and a more immersive feeling of the days in and out of the park. Our desire for players to have more connection with their dino best friends meant trying to ensure players felt the life cycle of their dinos, that you watched them grow each and every day. This was always our motivation for a day-night cycle. This also meant having an [b]end of day[/b].
After reading and listening to you, the players, we have heard your frustrations with the [b]end of day[/b]. We are implementing a LOT of changes to improve the [b]end of day[/b] experience. I’d like to chat about [b]UPCOMING[/b] changes:
[list]
[*] Toggle option to go directly into the next day!
[*] Integrating the Finance Wrap-up screen into the computer overview
[*] Remembering camera position
[*] Remembering tool selection
[*] Bright end of day warning
 [/list]

[h1]Toggle go directly into the next day![/h1]
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/LODsID6hzq8votseue/giphy.gif[/img]
That’s right. When the [b]end of day[/b] arrives a toggle option appears in the upper right portion of the screen. If the toggle is enabled your park will immediately go into a new day. Stock up on food and let the sim carry itself out. 😊

This post is a little offbeat. I thought it might be interesting to see how [i]Parksaurus[/i] has changed since entering Early Access. 

Every time a major tuning change is introduced into the game we run all-day simulations. Essentially this is for two reasons: 
[list]

[*] To see if the game tuning is having the desired effect
[*] To identify any unforeseen issues
 [/list]

In response to your feedback we started to tune this back, and then [b]REALLY[/b] tuned this far back – seen as the sharp drop. Too far! With more tuning, we slightly increased the money generation and feel pretty happy where we are now.

[h1]Garbage[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/49bde369ce9ceca691c9c1e4ba4495a12d8512e6.jpg[/img]
I find this graph a cool example of how our simulation system identifies problems. This graph shows how much [b]garbage[/b] an “average” park generated. notes.title: Breeding Preview
notes.notes:
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/Ka2PUB8Vvs74wQxpSA/giphy.gif[/img]

[b]Breeding[/b] dinosaurs in [i]Parkasaurus[/i] is on the way for the next patch. Breeding allows you to combine the color [b]characteristics[/b] and [b]personality traits[/b] of two dino parents together to create an offspring. In this exhibit we have two Kosmoceratops; Ollie and Matilda. They've been inseparable since a young age. 

Now we help them create a baby Kosmoceratops!

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/lnapvoJCchcJXlplil/giphy.gif[/img]
First, It all starts with an egg!

[b]Second, in order for two dinos to breed their respective Happiness must be above 80%.[/b]

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/ZG5NJS1FFitv2Mr3P2/giphy.gif[/img]
The egg is added! But, we need to ensure both Ollie and Matilda have their [b]Happiness[/b] above 80%. A great way to improve the [b]Happiness[/b] of your dinos is to improve the privacy of their exhibit by adding privacy grass to the viewing [b]hotspots[/b]. You know your dinos have achieved breeding happiness when their dino egg is glowing! This means breeding is currently underway.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/daOrbnNrkCMsFy54Ru/giphy.gif[/img]
We highly suggest creating a DNA machine. This helps you [b]Scan[/b] the new Kosmoceratops egg. Now you can adjust a slider to which parent you would like to inherit more DNA. You can see this adjusts the color of our baby along with other attributes such as scariness, love, and aggression. The unique [b]personality traits[/b] of the parents are also inherited by the baby dino.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/iiEczcpAHk1VALd7dC/giphy.gif[/img]
Finally, after anxiously waiting - Ollie and Matilda are proud parents of Rufus!

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/Ver2Mz3V3KHlZF6NAA/giphy.gif[/img]
Breeding dinos is a great economical way to add higher tier dinos to your park.

Also, we're releasing more campaign missions in the same patch, we'll have more to say about that later! Thanks all. xoxo

[*] Fences and Obstacles

 [/list]

[h1]Fences and Obstacles[/h1]
An idea that we enjoy exploring is constructing amazing dinosaur exhibits in weird & challenging areas. This has meant a lot of coding to ensure we solve for all the edge cases of where you can and cannot build. Here is a test of constructing an exhibit around city buildings.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/WTAIUM4Y6i7BEBz5sD/giphy.gif[/img]

[h1]Detailed reviews[/h1]
You might have noticed in [i]Parkasaurus[/i] that receiving a high park star rating, and high star user ratings can be difficult. We have decided to [b]expose[/b] all the values going into these calculations to help players determine at the end of the day where they can improve their dinosaur park. Also, there are still a few bugs with the review system – such as a tiny piece of garbage resulting in an over expression of guest dissatisfaction. 

 [img]https://media.giphy.com/media/SvFPkyjwbvbIhxHmxq/giphy.gif[/img]

[h1]One big family[/h1]
There has been some experimentation on how we could challenge players to have multi-biome exhibits without penalty (you can always have multi species exhibits with penalty) – if you have any suggestions be sure to leave a comment. [img] https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/75c3a179f149d5de7f2751476cdeef6ff5df7433.jpg [/img]
[h1]Update #28: Analytics[/h1]
Recently we’ve been getting [b]mods[/b] support ready for [i]Parkasaurus[/i] and hopefully will have a test version up on PTR this week.
A few people have asked us about a discount. Our response is that we feel the game is currently on a discount until more content (like a campaign, breeding, ++) is implemented and the price will slightly increase. We have no intention of putting the game on a discount until after 1.0; the main reason being our community who supports us in Early Access deserves the best-priced product for them taking the risk in believing in us. We don’t take that lightly. 
Blah blah blah, but what is this update about? Alright! Lot’s of background work:

[h1]Update:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Mod Preview
[*] Analytics
[/list]
[h1]Mod Preview[/h1]
We’re aiming to have a mod enabled version of [i]Parkasaurus[/i] up on PTR very soon. Currently you will be able to add [b]Dinosaurs[/b], [b]People[/b] and [b]Buildings[/b]. Implementing mods for the game has turned out to be more work than expected – hence you didn’t hear from us for a little while. Sorry about that!

 [img] https://i.imgur.com/faJfbI4.jpg [/img]

Today I was testing out some free assets from the Unity store and figured [i]“Hey what about a ship that serves fish and chips?”[/i]. Right? Well just so happens they had a free ship. I added our custom [b]building shader[/b] and wham bam we have a [b]ship store[/b] in Parkasaurus. 
Of course, [b]dinos[/b] and [b]people[/b] are presenting more of a challenge. Still, we persevere for the community!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/oldtnn5.gif[/img]

Now, to be clear, this is [b]NOT[/b] the Parkasaurus style, and I find it quite hum drum… but, a [i]“realistic”[/i] dino skin. (where are the feathers?)

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/cKPZzudoO5ffYXd7St/giphy.gif[/img]

Ok ok, I can maybe get a bit more on board for dino [b]party skin[/b]. 

[img] https://i.imgur.com/bj8OuiH.jpg[/img]

Now, rocket launchers on an Achelousaurus? GROW UP.

[h1] Analytics[/h1]
This might be less interesting to some, and more interesting to others. Recently more time has been spent looking at the newer systems we’ve implemented in the game – for example maintaining the energy of your guests. If your guest’s energy goes to 0, they leave the park. Seen below, we started to examine, [i]”Ok, should I see a difference between a park with no benches (energy refillers) versus a park with benches[/i]. 

[img] https://i.imgur.com/jMDF4yK.jpg[/img]

The top graph shows a histogram of the number of dinos seen by guests depending on if the park as benches or not. The park without benches clearly has a lower distribution of maximum dinos seen, a huge portion maxing at 11. The park with benches has a distribution of higher seen dinos, most notably a lot of guests who saw 13 dinos, then 14, 15 and 16. Great! This indicates the benches are extending the time guests spend at the park by maintaining their energy above 0.
The bottom graph demonstrates the difference between guests who have a total park allotment time of 0.4 vs 0.8, 1.0 being a [b]full day[/b] of time. Guests that have 0.4 total park time see no difference between a park with benches or without benches. This indicates to us the limiting factor is not guests running out of energy but rather running out of allocated park time. We will likely be tuning this a bit.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/dTjxCIl.jpg[/img]

Here we decided to examine a few basic metrics to ensure we didn’t have issues with our guests going into idle too often. [b]graph top-left[/b] Shows us the total amount donated by guest depending on the number of dinos they’ve seen. As you can expect, the more dinos seen the more guests donate. Of course, there seems to be a plateau around 12 that we’re looking into. Any ideas? [b]graph top-right[/b] We were worried that guests were [b]chilling[/b] (a random idle) too often, but see that the average donated by guests seems fairly consistent regardless of their chill totals. [b]graph bottom-left[/b] We also were worried that doing non-dino activities (like shopping) was consuming too much a guest's allocated park time, and again this was not the case. [b]graph bottom-right[/b]Finally it was interesting to see the actual distribution of chills per guests during their visits. Some guests chilled 26 times? Talk about taking it easy. Anyway, from all of this we’re hoping to push the [b]perk system[/b] into a more meaningful gameplay experience.

To all the [b]early supporters[/b] who have helped us in [b]Early Access[/b] thanks again. We have a long journey ahead of us and you motivate us each and every day.

Hello [i]Parkasaurus[/i] friends! I’m happy to share with you some details of the [b]Dino Money & Items[/b] Update (v0.620) that is currently live and what is coming up next. First, let’s chat about the major changes in [b]v0.620[/b].

[h1]Dino Money & Items v0.620[/h1]
[list]
[*] Carnotaurus
[*] Hats!!!
[*] Doors
[*] Decoration System Overhaul
[*] Portal Overhaul
[*] Economy Balancing
[*] Guest Meters
[*] News moving forward
 [/list]
[h1]Carnotaurus[/h1]
What can we say? There are already more Theropods in the game than any other dino family but the Call for the Carno (C4C) was too strong. Of course, getting your hands on a Carnotaurus is no easy feat in regular play. What will your adult Carno look like? And more importantly, what sort of sun protection will they have? Be sure to share with us.
[img] https://media.giphy.com/media/mCD17yUy9RoMloPHN7/giphy.gif[/img]

 [h1]Hats!!! [/h1]
SO MANY HATS. Here is the thing, you [b]won’t find them in the store[/b]. What?! You need to get a shovel, and, some real cash flow, to dig into the depths of the Earth. New hats will only be available from [b]Hat Treasure Boxes[/b] found when digging in the portal. Hopefully, someone out there will create an exhaustive list of the new hats added (hint: there are 12).
[img]https://i.imgur.com/WRhzBuu.jpg[/img]

[h1]Doors[/h1] 
Even we have to agree that only have 1 boring [b]Wooden Door[/b] was getting old. Since you’re all a creative bunch we wanted to give you some options on cooler ways to let employees enter the [b]exhibits[/b]. 
[img] https://media.giphy.com/media/l1TqOpdZT7fFeyXhKr/giphy.gif[/img]

[h1]Decoration System Overhaul[/h1]
The present [b]Decoration System[/b] in the game was not particularly interesting and truthfully was never given the time it deserved. Now strategically placing your decorations matter. Your guests enter your park with a value of 0 for their [b]Decoration[/b] meter. This meter slowly fills as they are surrounded by your awesome park extras. How can you tell what your park [b]decorations[/b] look like? Well, turn on the [b]Decoration Heatmap View[/b] found on the bottom left. Note, [b]Tier 2[/b] decorations need to be researched and bought in order to max out your guest’s decoration meters. 
[img] https://media.giphy.com/media/chz0erAHgO1LvHqYtK/giphy.gif[/img]	

[h1]Portal Overhaul[/h1]
The [b]portal[/b] has received some love. A few highlights:
[list]
[*] Auto-Dig added (but at a price!) 
[*] Select how deep into the [b]portal[/b] you’d like to go; the deeper the better [b]rewards[/b]!
[*] Choose a portal team from a list of your employees
[*] Portal rewards – now find Hat Boxes, Science, and Hearts along with the original [b]rewards[/b]!
[/list]
[img] https://media.giphy.com/media/SqO0aI15Xa4k5aprG1/giphy.gif[/img]

[h1] Economy Balancing[/h1]
This no doubt will be a contentious change. But our community is so amazing I look forward to hearing their feedback. Remember when money was really easy to make? We’ve been analyzing data from our great PTR volunteers and now challenge you to the new balanced [b]Parkasaurus Economy[/b]! For those of you less interested in having to balance the books and would rather focus on creativity – don’t worry you can still make a [b]Customized[/b] game.
[img] https://i.imgur.com/Y3I8R0Sh.jpg[/img]

[h1]Guest Meters [/h1]
A more subtle change involves the guest [b]meters[/b]. You’ll note that the [b]energy meter[/b] has been pulled out of what contributes to your guest’s overall [b]happiness[/b]. Now keeping your guests energized is an important aspect of keeping them in the park. By doing this we were able to remove the “decaying” that occurred with the remaining meters; something that was anxious inducing (for me) and also resulted in your guests draining their meters while walking to their cars at the end of the day – thereby lowering park scores & review stars. 
[img] https://i.imgur.com/IcgbBbSh.jpg[/img]

[h1] News moving forward[/h1]
Again – huge thanks to the [b]early supporters[/b] and everyone who has written a [b]Steam review[/b] for us. Next on the horizon:
[*] Mods (this features it 90% done, and we will be revealing more shortly)
[*] Bugs! Sometimes you might not hear from us for a little while, that’s because there are still a bunch of bugs in the game
[*] Price increase

I would like to talk briefly about a price increase. We’ve always felt it important to value the game at what we think it is worth. As we add more features the price of the game will likely go up a small amount to account for this. Also – we feel it a nice [b]Thank You[/b] for early adopters. Now, we aren’t doing this today, but we want to give you a heads up long before this happens. 
Again, thanks to our amazing, amazing community.

Thanks. xoxo

notes.title: Update #26: House Cleaning
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/c4fc036c542a40c1cc57633314a5421f7beb9869.jpg[/img]

[h1]House Cleaning[/h1]
Hello our Dino family! First – we hope everyone is doing healthy and well in this New Year. This is a quick Update, and truthfully, maybe unexciting for many of you. With that said we wanted to continue our transparency with the community. 

We decided to do a major pass on some of our worst offending bugs, and then do a first pass update on the economy before implementing [b]Mods[/b]. Now, the technical work for [b]Mods[/b] has been completed and ready to go; it just felt wrong bringing new players into a game that had gained quite a few bugs since release. The challenge of adding new features is that one usually adds more bugs. This Update is termed [i]House Cleaning[/i] because that’s what we’re doing, cleaning/fixing up the [i]Parkasaurus[/i] house before putting in an updated economy and [b]Mods[/b]. 

We appreciated your amazing support and understanding during this recent bug fixing stage. On the outside, the bugs don’t look like much, but on the inside, they are a lot for the game! Here are a few of the more random bugs we fixed:

[h1]Update:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Great view up here!
[*] This park is … dirty
[*] Kentro-Sharks
[/list]

[h1] Great view up here![/h1]
Turns out with the update to our custom Navigation system that the collisions within the roofs of many buildings was being seen as [b]walkable[/b] terrain. This resulted in your employees thinking they could walk up high, and never being able to get down because of the elevation difference. Case in point:
[img] https://i.imgur.com/7jDkp6w.jpg[/img]

[h1]This park is … dirty [/h1]
We started getting reports of people’s parks being over-run with garbage. Well, that’s exactly what was happening. Our logic system for the janitors calculates all the tasks in their immediate surroundings, ranks them, and usually chooses one to do. This works most of the time. But there turned out to be a [b]tipping point[/b] of garbage pieces (messy guests) where your janitor would become paralyzed with deciding what plastic wrapper or can to pick up. The result was them becoming confused and picking nothing up, leading to more garbage, leading to more confusion.
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/495ME2xgiaClEgRo0q/giphy.gif [/img]

[h1]Kentro-Sharks[/h1] 
Do you ever hate it when your [b]Kentrosaurus[/b] become [b]Kentro-Sharks[/b]? An elevation bug for our dino friends entered the game where nobody really knew where their feet belonged. This resulted in dinos walking too high (especially new born babies) and also way too low. I will admit the scales swimming around the park looked cool, but unfortunately not practical. 
[img]https://i.imgur.com/qF0LmLT.jpg[/img]

To all you [b]early supporters[/b] – thanks a ton. Don’t worry, we’re still thinking of something awesome to give everyone who has helped us in [b]Early Access[/b]. Also, owning the game already means the price can never go up for you :)

[h1] Performance Optimizations[/h1]
If you find [i]performance optimization[/i] as interesting as we do – then this is what’s new. First, the guests to your park had a new AI overhaul, so no more standing around figuring out where to go. This originally wasn’t a problem for small parks, but many of you reported guest clumping and lag at higher guest counts. This combined with a more efficient mesh navigation system should result in performance improvements for many of you. Now, these improvements in [b]theory[/b] should be more noticeable for those of you who are CPU bottlenecked instead of GPU bottlenecked. [h1]MOD Preview[/h1]
Hi Friends! Where have we been you ask! Let me catch you all up. The two major tasks we’ve been working on is performance and workshop/mods. Now, we understand there is some serious game re-balancing, and bug fixes that are still to be done – but – from a technical perspective we would save a lot of work doing the performance improvements first for [i]Parkasaurus[/i]. And the thing about performance work is that I rarely have any cool pictures to show. BUT, performance work also means us getting very close to implementing [b] workshop/mods [/b] into the game. I’d like to reveal a little of what is to come:

[h1]Update:[/h1]

[list]
[*] MOD: Dino Textures
[*] MOD: Dino Meshes (body)
[*] MOD: Swap-able buildings
[*] New mystery dino

notes.title: Adorable dinosaur park management sim Parkasaurus is out now on Steam Early Access
notes.notes:
Developer WashBear Studio's unashamedly adorable dinosaur theme park management sim Parkasaurus is now available in Steam Early Access - and it's already shaping up to be something a bit special.

I've admittedly only managed to get a few hours of prehistoric creature wrangling under my belt so far, but Parkasaurus - which takes obvious inspiration from the likes of Theme Park and DinoPark Tycoon - arrives with a frankly astonishing degree of polish for an early access title.

The core of the whole thing is, of course, the dinosaurs that you'll be hatching from eggs and displaying proudly to hopefully paying customers, and there's already a decent selection of creatures to bring home. Each dinosaur has specific needs to meet - a favoured ecosystem (which you'll have to recreate from scratch by adjusting terrain types, water levels, and scenery), as well as privacy requirements, food preferences, socialisation, and more - giving you plenty to think about even before the rest of the park comes into play.

Hi Dino friends! The time has come for [i]Parkasaurus[/i] to enter Early Access. 

First off the two of us who make up the [i]Parkasaurus[/i] team want to [b]thank everyone[/b] who playtested, gave us feedback, told their friends or forums about us, or just hung out in Discord and was awesome. We hope the [i]Parkasaurus[/i] family gets bigger today, and with that comes a new group of people to help choose the direction of where we go. Yes – the next few weeks will likely be fixing terrible bugs and game balancing, but it also will be an opportunity to hear feedback from everyone and update our roadmap. Not to stray too far from our usual updates, I just wanted to provide a little background to [i]Parkasaurus[/i] and then some fun stuff. 

[h1]The Origin of Parkasaurus[/h1]
We thought it would be fun to share the origin of how we came to start making Parkasaurus. Although the game nods to previous games before it, the impetuous came from a handmade game design doc in the form of a colorful binder that is called DinoGame, with sparkles and all. DinoBook was split by tabs into categories, detailing how a dino tycoon sim game could work. Well – thanks to one of our wives, we fell in love with the idea of DinoGame and ran with it.

[list]
[*] Wandering your park at night
[*] No You Clean the Toilet
[*] Food Court Design
[*] Dinos with Style
[/list]


[h1] Wandering your park at night [/h1]
Spending the entire Parkasaurus day can sometimes be stressful, especially if you get a breakout. I like to take the time and use the free cam to enjoy the cool views at night.
[img=https://media.giphy.com/media/fngk0VZsV5ZOF5qG2u/giphy.gif]
	

[h1] No You Clean the Toilet [/h1] 
In Parkasaurus the employees automatically will try to find tasks to do around the park. You can toggle them to just do one task if you want (eg. [img=https://i.imgur.com/IbjCZNz.png]


[h1] Food Court Design [/h1] 
There is a lot of emphasis on Exhibit Design in Parkasaurus, and for good reason. Happy Dinos mean more money to expand your park. But it also is fun to take your time and plan how you’ll create little food courts around your park. 
[img=https://media.giphy.com/media/psmQv592OEYsvYsP7k/giphy.gif]


[h1] Dinos with Style [/h1] 
Perhaps most importantly in Parkasaurus you’ll need to equip your dinos to look good. Your dino best friends won’t be able to wear accessories until they become adults; so that gives you plenty of time to research and stock up on the coolest items in town.

[h1]Parkasaurus Update #018 : The Pursuit of Raptorness[/h1]

[i]Parkasaurus[/i] is humming right along. We’re feeling pretty happy with our complete re-do of the starting tutorial, and now are focusing on gameplay after 7+ days of [b]park time[/b]. This includes income balancing which is a pretty big challenge at the moment, with only two of us it can be hard to get in a 2-hour game session. 😊 But! Have no fear, we know soon the community will be helping us out (hopefully) with balance, and providing great suggestions on what needs to change. We’ve already had some pretty cool suggestions on our Discord and Roadmap (all links below)

[h1] Update 018 Topics[/h1]
[list]
[*] See in the dark
[*] Pack Hunting
[*] Fence Fun
[*] Bonus: Experimental Terrain Generator
[/list]

[h1] See in the dark [/h1]
We added in some more interesting [b]streetlights[/b] to give the player some more options when designing their park at night. My favorite is the [b]string lights[/b] that attached from tall scenery objects in your park to other tall objects. This meant having to go through all our park build-ables and add the appropriate collisions which is a time-consuming process…but well worth it; I think. (I better of thought that since I had to do it)
[img=https://media.giphy.com/media/ujTVigdQd2xx4luxCX/giphy.gif]

[h1] Pack Hunting [/h1]
In order to push our dino behavior a little farther, Velociraptors pack hunt when trying to attack a large dino in their exhibit. They intentionally try to walk through the tall grass before the attack (any dino in tall grass gets a reduction to their "view-ability" from a guest or other dinos. It might be fun for them to pack hunt guests also, perhaps I’ll try that next.
[img=https://i.imgur.com/AJ4nxCQ.png]

[h1] Fence Fun [/h1]
Whipping up a bare-bones exhibit to test our new range of fence materials including an overhaul on icons, values, and imagery. Fence materials affect the [b]viewability[/b] of the exhibit from the view point of the guests, and perhaps, more importantly, the [b]strength[/b] of the fence. A stronger fence means less repair work for your [b]janitors[/b] or allows you to keep in some pretty scary best dino friends.
[img=https://media.giphy.com/media/DQaWg7EjC9YB45toPY/giphy.gif]

notes.title: Amazing News : we decided make Parkasaurus GREAT (by pushing EA)
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/7e81db4aa1f22deae6a944b6a8b66dad25651b6f.png[/img]

Hi there Parkasaurus best friends. 

When the two of us started Parkasaurus a promise was made to ourselves to never release our game into Early Access before we felt it was ready. Too many times we’ve personally supported Kickstarters, and Early Access games that have release broken, and then disappear into the night. I understand all too well how hard it is to make games – but I also know that gamers who amazingly buy Early Access to support me, who give me money saying “we believe in this product and YOU”, deserve a tight working game experience. 

We know that you are all excited for the game and we can't wait to let you get your hands on Parkasaurus and to see what parks and exhibits you create for your dino best friends.

Unfortunately during our evaluation process we feel that, whilst progressing at lightning speed, the game isn't yet early access ready in a way that you deserve, and we do not want to rush something out just to meet our forecast Spring window. Many people have told us it is crazy to not release very soon – that from a business perspective this is suicide. We don’t care – what we care about most is an Early Access game we can be proud of, and a game we can develop together with you, early supporters, to eventually release the best Parkasaurus can be.

Pushing our early access release by a few months means that we are able to refine what we already have and introduce some other, as yet unannounced, features to the game. We have a crystal clear roadmap to bring Parkasaurus to Early Access and then far far beyond, to a 1.0 release, and then much more. Come with us on the ride!

Our regular updates continue as usual and we will continue to be active in the [url=https://discord.gg/mGWpeRg]Discord[/url] server  and other social channels, bringing polls, providing idea submission forms and asking for feedback on features as they are implemented.

Howdy [b]Parkasaurus Warriors[/b]™. Apologies for this update being 1 day late; we were busy getting ready for the most romantic day of the year: February 15th - Galileo Day! The day when we celebrate our love of dinosaurs and all topics science. Here is your [i]Parkasaurus[/i] Update #005. 

[h1]Alpha Version 2 – Closer still…[/h1]
This was a very exciting week. Topics to chat about from least exciting to most: we created some cool [b]shaders[/b] to give the plants and fauna more life,  developed robust [b]management graphs[/b] for the in-game office computer and lastly started our first [b]playtests[/b] with close friends. As you can imagine it was exciting and scary! One of our playtests ended when the water flooded the park…

[h1]Update 005 Topics[/h1]
[list]
[*]Plant Shaders
[*]Management Analysis System
[*]Playtests
[/list]

[h1]Plant Shaders [/h1]
A core dimension for us when creating [i]Parksaurus[/i] is to emphasize the importance of using appropriate fauna in your best friend Dino exhibits. This is why we strive to do everything we can to help make the worlds you design more beautiful. Our newest shader does just that; giving life -like wind motion to all the plants in the [i]Parksaurus[/i] world, using a 2d noise map that moves across the world. The amount of wind varies with the time of day, time of year and the width & height of the plants. It looks great:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/b33e38e0c4650140f4c216b77cea8813d9e8099a.gif[/img]

[h1]Management Analysis System[/h1]
In [i]Parksaurus[/i] you’ll have the chance to retire to your office to examine the park budget; where did you lose money? Which of your best friend Dinos generates the most money from the guests? Did curly fries sell more than waffles fries on Thursdays? Management graphs were put into the office computer so you can check revenue, profit, etc. throughout the days. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/cb9e94755e8d71938aeb71c51e876c57beeeb4b1.gif[/img]


[h1]Playtests[/h1]
The first playtests occurred last week to much terror and excitement. Mostly terror? As predicted the playtests were … interesting. One always wants a raving success when the first people try out your game; the reality is usually tears. Luckily we’ve gone through enough playtests to know the roller coaster of emotions. Ok, joking aside we learned a lot. Our favourite game ending bug though was water leaking out of a Sauropod exhibit and slowly but surely flooding an entire park on Day 7. Good times:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/f7963b8b6aa0513344de5d62b991e265c05199c6.gif[/img]

Howdy [b]Parkasaurus Warriors[/b]. 2018 has begun and both MT and I hope you’re doing great. One of us got the flu but has fully recovered. Alrighty, down to business.

[h1]Alpha Version 2[/h1]
Everything looks to be on track. We might take an extra week to reach Alpha Ver 2 in order to give a thorough pass on Dino logic. Specifically carnivore behavior – we’re looking to make their demeanor more personable; ie. more like lions at the zoo as opposed to berserk monsters from the movies. (don’t worry, they still eat people)

 [h1]Update 003 Topics[/h1]
[list]
[*]Bio-Diversity 
[*]Preview Tool
[*]Upgrade Sets
[/list]

[h1]Bio-Diversity[/h1]
We’re hoping players create beautiful diverse exhibits for their Dinos that include a range of fauna and decoration. The earlier version of bio-diversity tried to reward players to achieve the perfect balance between trees : rocks : plants. After designing a few exhibits we quickly found this system stifled the creativity of players. Not cool!  Instead we reward players for bio-diversity, but don’t punish players if this is not their prime focus in [i]Parkasaurus[/i]. Much better.  The bars shown in the image now indicate the amount of each fauna / decoration type in the selected exhibit, and also how many of level 1 types versus level 2 types. Level 2 exhibit type items are researched and give bonuses to Dino happiness among other cool benefits. 
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/e5b12c2cb5874717f9834612d856cd62e0f823ea.gif[/img]

[h1]Preview Tool[/h1]
This maybe isn’t the most exciting picture to show – but it is the most exciting for me to work with! We created a tool to create awesome preview pictures (right) for the in-game build menu based off the original 3D models (left). What this means for [i]Parkasaurus[/i]  is 1) beautiful preview images 2) keeps us on pace to get the game into your hands.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/e23244a109b296b539f9342f0b370fd8aaf000f2.png[/img]

Hello Steam friends. 

I was hoping to start posting an update every few weeks to a) let everyone know what we’re up to b) let you know we’re still alive. Now – apologies if these posts are on the lean side – since there are only 2 of us on this game I might not spend as much time writing this as wish I could. Still, updating all of you is probably #1 on my “TODO” list so time will be found!

[h1]Alpha Version 2[/h1]
MT and I have Alpha Version 2 (AV2) as our next major milestone. Basically this means we’ve put a hold on adding new features and going back through older features to make them more awesome. With that said I’m sure MT will ninja in a few features as we go along.

[h1]Update 001 Topics[/h1]
A few select topics we worked on recently:
[list]
    [*]Exhibit Privacy System
    [*]Dynamic Water
    [*]Dino Skins (Shader)
[/list]

[h1]Exhibit Privacy System[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/087e82f7a724fe72016b61de3be94fb33c3b7de0.jpg[/img]
An important aspect of designing your Dino exhibit(s) is privacy. Your Dino friends are affected by privacy; now, some Dino species are more resilient to hoards of guests gawking at them; but all of your Dinos require some down time. How much privacy your exhibit has depends on the shape of your exhibit, materials used around and within your exhibit among other factors. In the picture above is an exhibit demonstrating privacy: the privacy toggle is on so you see a [b]privacy heatmap[/b] within the exhibit showing what parts are private, and what parts are not private. Understandably areas near guest viewing areas (paths) are not private, so you can immediately see how you decide to design your exhibit directly impacts on your Dino’s privacy.

[h1]Dynamic Water[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/36f12c7789430f792f0001608d9fbdc8a28d1415.gif[/img]
We now have moving water! First it looks [b]cool[/b]. :) More importantly though, water is an essential aspect of your exhibit. The amount of water in your exhibit transforms the type of biosphere thereby being more suitable for one type of Dino species versus another. Water also dictates what types of trees, plants & rocks you can successfully grow in your exhibit. 

[h1] Dino Skins (Shader) [/h1]
We really want people to see each of their Dinos as unique and special. Therefor we made a cool [b]shader[/b] (a shader is a special piece of programming code that does something specific with game graphics) that gives the skin of each Dino a unique look and color scheme. I probably linked the least cool of the results I’ve seen for far in the game, but it hopefully gives you an idea.

[h1]Thanks to all you early Parkasaurus Warriors[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/b08c1f593114cd7cd85c806bc9ecae4042345d40.jpg[/img]

[h1]Exhibit Privacy System[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/087e82f7a724fe72016b61de3be94fb33c3b7de0.jpg[/img]
An important aspect of designing your Dino exhibit(s) is privacy. Your Dino friends are affected by privacy; now, some Dino species are more resilient to hoards of guests gawking at them; but all of your Dinos require some down time. How much privacy your exhibit has depends on the shape of your exhibit, materials used around and within your exhibit among other factors. In the picture above is an exhibit demonstrating privacy: the privacy toggle is on so you see a [b]privacy heatmap[/b] within the exhibit showing what parts are private, and what parts are not private. Understandably areas near guest viewing areas (paths) are not private, so you can immediately see how you decide to design your exhibit directly impacts on your Dino’s privacy.

[h1]Dynamic Water[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/36f12c7789430f792f0001608d9fbdc8a28d1415.gif[/img]
We now have moving water! First it looks [b]cool[/b]. :) More importantly though, water is an essential aspect of your exhibit. The amount of water in your exhibit transforms the type of biosphere thereby being more suitable for one type of Dino species versus another. Water also dictates what types of trees, plants & rocks you can successfully grow in your exhibit.
